ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $I$ is the incenter of $\triangle ABC$, $O$ is a point on side $AB$, and $\odot O$ passes through point $B$ and is tangent to $AI$ at point $I$. If $\tan\angle BAC = \frac{24}{7}$, then what is the value of $\sin\angle ACB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, extend line OI to intersect AC at D and connect BI.\\
$\because$ AI is tangent to the circle with center O,\\
$\therefore$ AI $\perp$ OD,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$AIO = $\angle$AID = $90^\circ$,\\
$\because$ I is the incenter of $\triangle ABC$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$OAI = $\angle$DAI, $\angle$ABI = $\angle$CBI,\\
$\because$ AI = AI,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle AOI \cong \triangle ADI$ (ASA),\\
$\therefore$ AO = AD,\\
$\because$ OB = OI,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$OBI = $\angle$OIB,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$OIB = $\angle$CBI,\\
$\therefore$ OD $\parallel$ BC,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$ADO = $\angle$C,\\
Construct OE $\perp$ AC at E,\\
$\because$ $\tan\angle$BAC = $\frac{OE}{AE}$ = $\frac{24}{7}$,\\
$\therefore$ assume OE = 24k, AE = 7k without loss of generality,\\
$\therefore$ OA = AD = 25k,\\
$\therefore$ DE = AD - AE = 18k,\\
$\therefore$ OD = $\sqrt{OE^2 + DE^2}$ = 30k,\\
$\therefore$ $\sin\angle$ACB = $\frac{OE}{OD}$ = $\frac{24k}{30k}$ = $\boxed{\frac{4}{5}}$.

method.method_draft: Use the standard synthetic length construction. From the diagram, extend the radius line OI until it meets AC at D, and draw BI. Since the circle centered at O is tangent to AI at I, OI is perpendicular to AI. Because I is the incenter, AI bisects angle A and BI bisects angle B. Thus triangles AOI and ADI are congruent by ASA, giving AO = AD. Also OB = OI as radii of the same circle, so triangle OBI is isosceles; combine this with BI being the angle bisector at B to get OI parallel to BC, hence OD parallel to BC and angle ADO equals angle ACB. Drop OE perpendicular to AC. Since O lies on AB and AC is the reference side, tan angle BAC = OE/AE = 24/7, so set AE = 7k and OE = 24k. Then AO = 25k, so AD = 25k, DE = 18k, and OD = sqrt((18k)^2 + (24k)^2) = 30k. Because OD is parallel to BC, sin angle ACB = sin angle ADO = OE/OD = 24/30 = 4/5.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中是三角形 ABC，A 在上方，B 在左下方，C 在右下方，BC 近似水平。点 O 位于边 AB 上，点 I 在三角形内部且在从 A 出发的角平分线附近；以 O 为圆心的圆经过 B，并在 I 处与直线 AI 相切。

推理：按题设与构造，延长 OI 交 AC 于 D，并连接 BI。因为圆心为 O 的圆在 I 点与 AI 相切，所以半径 OI 垂直于 AI，即 ∠AIO = 90°，且 D 在 OI 的延长线上，所以 ∠AID = 90°。I 是内心，因此 AI 平分 ∠A，BI 平分 ∠B；又 O 在 AB 上、D 在 AC 上，所以 ∠OAI = ∠DAI。结合 AI 公共边，△AOI 与 △ADI 由 ASA 全等，因此 AO = AD。

又因为圆经过 B 且 I 是切点，所以 OB = OI，△OBI 为等腰三角形，故 ∠OBI = ∠OIB。由于 O 在 AB 上，∠OBI = ∠ABI；又 BI 平分 ∠ABC，所以 ∠ABI = ∠CBI。于是 ∠OIB = ∠CBI，推出 OD ∥ BC。因此 ∠ADO = ∠ACB。

过 O 作 OE ⟂ AC，垂足为 E。因为 O 在 AB 上、E 在 AC 上，所以 ∠OAE = ∠BAC，且在直角三角形 AOE 中，tan∠BAC = OE/AE = 24/7。令 AE = 7k，OE = 24k，则 AO = sqrt((7k)^2 + (24k)^2) = 25k。由 AO = AD 得 AD = 25k，所以 DE = AD - AE = 18k。于是 OD = sqrt((18k)^2 + (24k)^2) = 30k。因为 OD ∥ BC，所以 sin∠ACB = sin∠ADO = OE/OD = 24k/30k = 4/5。

又因为圆经过 B 且 I 是切点，所以 OB = OI，△OBI 为等腰三角形，故 ∠OBI = ∠OIB。由于 O 在 AB 上，∠OBI = ∠ABI；又 BI 平分 ∠ABC，所以 ∠ABI = ∠CBI。于是 ∠OIB = ∠CBI，推出 OD ∥ BC。因此 ∠ADO = ∠ACB。

过 O 作 OE ⟂ AC，垂足为 E。因为 O 在 AB 上、E 在 AC 上，所以 ∠OAE = ∠BAC，且在直角三角形 AOE 中，tan∠BAC = OE/AE = 24/7。令 AE = 7k，OE = 24k，则 AO = sqrt((7k)^2 + (24k)^2) = 25k。由 AO = AD 得 AD = 25k，所以 DE = AD - AE = 18k。于是 OD = sqrt((18k)^2 + (24k)^2) = 30k。因为 OD ∥ BC，所以 sin∠ACB = sin∠ADO = OE/OD = 24k/30k = 4/5。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $I$ is the incenter of $\triangle ABC$, $O$ is a point on side $AB$, and $\odot O$ passes through point $B$ and is tangent to $AI$ at point $I$. If $\tan\angle BAC = \frac{24}{7}$, then what is the value of $\sin\angle ACB$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, extend line OI to intersect AC at D and connect BI.\\
$\because$ AI is tangent to the circle with center O,\\
$\therefore$ AI $\perp$ OD,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$AIO = $\angle$AID = $90^\circ$,\\
$\because$ I is the incenter of $\triangle ABC$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$OAI = $\angle$DAI, $\angle$ABI = $\angle$CBI,\\
$\because$ AI = AI,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle AOI \cong \triangle ADI$ (ASA),\\
$\therefore$ AO = AD,\\
$\because$ OB = OI,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$OBI = $\angle$OIB,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$OIB = $\angle$CBI,\\
$\therefore$ OD $\parallel$ BC,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$ADO = $\angle$C,\\
Construct OE $\perp$ AC at E,\\
$\because$ $\tan\angle$BAC = $\frac{OE}{AE}$ = $\frac{24}{7}$,\\
$\therefore$ assume OE = 24k, AE = 7k without loss of generality,\\
$\therefore$ OA = AD = 25k,\\
$\therefore$ DE = AD - AE = 18k,\\
$\therefore$ OD = $\sqrt{OE^2 + DE^2}$ = 30k,\\
$\therefore$ $\sin\angle$ACB = $\frac{OE}{OD}$ = $\frac{24k}{30k}$ = $\boxed{\frac{4}{5}}$

Point O is located on side AB, point I is inside the triangle and near the angle bisector starting from A; the circle with O as center passes through B, and is tangent to line AI at I.

Reasoning: According to the conditions and construction, extend OI to meet AC at D, and connect BI. Because the circle with center O is tangent to AI at point I, the radius OI is perpendicular to AI, that is, ∠AIO = 90°, and D is on the extension of OI, so ∠AID = 90°. I is the incenter, therefore AI bisects ∠A, and BI bisects ∠B; also O is on AB and D is on AC, so ∠OAI = ∠DAI. Combining the common side AI, △AOI and △ADI are congruent by ASA, therefore AO = AD.

Also because the circle passes through B and I is the point of tangency, OB = OI, and △OBI is an isosceles triangle, hence ∠OBI = ∠OIB. Since O is on AB, ∠OBI = ∠ABI; also BI bisects ∠ABC, so ∠ABI = ∠CBI. Thus ∠OIB = ∠CBI, which gives OD ∥ BC. Therefore ∠ADO = ∠ACB.

Draw OE ⟂ AC through O, with foot E. Because O is on AB and E is on AC, ∠OAE = ∠BAC, and in the right triangle AOE, tan∠BAC = OE/AE = 24/7.
